output.brief: The rejects come from an interaction. Arnholt resin arrives wetter (0.27–0.33% against a 0.20% limit), and the Press 5 dryer (D5) is degraded, so it can't dry that resin enough. Neither factor alone causes the problem. Arnholt on Press 7 (good dryer) rejects 0.8%. Quillan on Press 5 rejects 0.9%. Arnholt through D5 rejects about 10%. The same Arnholt lot dried in a good portable dryer and run on Press 5 rejected 0.8%, against 10.4% through D5. The new operators are not the cause: second shift only looks worse because it runs only Press 5. Within Press 5, the new and experienced operators have the same rates on each resin. Don't put them on improvement plans. I'm fairly sure of this. The one gap is that Arnholt was stored only in the north annex, so supplier and storage are mixed together. That doesn't change what to do this week. Repair D5 (heater and desiccant), restore its −15 alarm limit to the original, keep Arnholt off D5 until D5 is verified at −40 °C, and check feed-throat moisture on every lot. Treat moving Arnholt out of the annex as a later question, and ask Arnholt about their moisture.
